svg.title: Canada Life IDP physical architecture and Azure landing zone
svg.desc: Four-view board showing Azure tenant hierarchy, subscriptions, Canada East production topology, Canada Central disaster recovery, non-production separation, delivery and operations.

text.tspan: Canada Life IDP — Azure Landing Zone
Tenant hierarchy, subscriptions, ownership and inherited guardrails
IDP is classified as a regulated
• Canada East and Canada Central hub VNets
• ExpressRoute/VPN, Azure Firewall Premium, Bastion, Private DNS Resolver
• DDoS Network Protection plan and network monitoring
• Log Analytics, Sentinel, Automation, Monitor Private Link Scope
• central immutable audit storage, Defender plans, policy remediation
• primary and DR workload stamps, production data and integration services
• development, test and performance environments; no production data
Owner: Central IT IDP Platform Team
Optional dedicated subscriptions can be added for exceptionally regulated LOBs
Allowed regions: Canada East / Canada Central • Deny public network access on data services • Require private endpoints and diagnostic settings
Require managed identity, TLS 1.2+, approved SKUs, CMK on document/data stores, tags, budgets and resource locks • Defender for Cloud enabled
AKS: private cluster, Entra RBAC, Azure Policy, workload identity, network policy, approved registries and signed images • Exceptions require expiry,
Illustrative addresses; final ranges require Canada Life enterprise IPAM approval
Application Gateway / internal ingress; end-to-end TLS
API Management Premium; internal/private APIs only
Private AKS system node pool; cluster services and ingress
Web/API pool • elastic worker pool • connector/ingestion pool
Availability Zones • HPA • cluster autoscaler • pod
Private endpoints for Blob, Service Bus, Key
Vault, ACR, Monitor, Content Understanding and Atlas PrivateLink
Private self-hosted integration runtime / managed connectors
All non-local egress follows UDR → Azure Firewall. AKS API
Channel → Canada Life private network → internal APIM → quarantine Blob → Defender/DLP release → Service Bus → AKS worker → Content Understanding → Atlas result
Quality gate → straight-through delivery or native review queue → API / Service Bus topic / Event Grid / batch exchange → downstream claims and case
Every hop uses managed identity or Entra token, private DNS/private endpoint where applicable, tenant/process/correlation context, and centralized
Canada Central warm standby plus isolated non-production landing zone
Scale target is proven by DR load testing,
REGIONAL FAILOVER — PLANNING TARGET RTO 4 HOURS / RPO 15 MINUTES
Declare and authorize failover → freeze nonessential writes → verify replication point → promote Atlas/Storage and regional integration
Scale DR AKS and APIM → update private DNS and internal routes → recreate incomplete Service Bus work from durable job state → validate
Quarterly technical failover, annual business continuity exercise, and post-test evidence are mandatory. Failback is a separate controlled
Entire Solution — Workloads, Delivery, Operations and Ownership
How the platform is built, governed, observed and consumed at enterprise scale
showback for pages, storage, AI and
• Shared enterprise landing zone services are separated from the IDP workload subscriptions; production and non-production never share data-plane
• No internet-facing application endpoint is deployed. Application ingress, AKS, data stores, keys, registry, monitoring and AI use private connectivity.
• Business-unit tenant ID is enforced consistently in identity claims, APIM policy, queue/session metadata, Atlas collections, Blob paths, quotas and
• CIDRs, SKUs and capacity are planning defaults. Final approval requires enterprise IPAM, dependency quotas, performance tests, threat modelling and DR
• Content Understanding in Canada is a future-state assumption and explicit production launch gate until Microsoft regional availability is verified.
